metadata.note: The Chicago, Burlington & Quincy's Omaha-Lincoln-Denver main line, built by its Burlington & Missouri River Railroad in Nebraska subsidiary. This is the western continuation of the CB&Q corridor in burlington_route_chicago_omaha.geojson, and the same physical line the Exposition Flyer and California Zephyr later ran (see california_zephyr_historical.geojson, which picks it up in 1939). Route geometry is the Omaha-Denver portion of Amtrak's own GTFS-sourced California Zephyr alignment, since the historical trains ran the same line. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Burlington and Missouri River Railroad, Denver Zephyr, Ak-Sar-Ben Zephyr), history.nebraska.gov, legendsofamerica.com, hmdb.org
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The Burlington & Missouri River Railroad in Nebraska, chartered 1869, began building from Plattsmouth in July 1869 and reached Lincoln - the newly designated state capital - in the summer of 1870, giving Lincoln its first rail connection. (Full Omaha-Denver route shown regardless of the year each section opened.) estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: Built west to join the Union Pacific at Kearney Junction Sept 3 1872, linking southern Nebraska traffic to the transcontinental route. In 1872 chief engineer Thomas Doane had 750,000 trees planted along 100 miles of this line between Lincoln and Lowell as a snow-drift barrier. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: All sections west to Denver were completed May 29 1882, and by that July the CB&Q was running regular Chicago-Denver service through Lincoln and McCook - the first direct rail line between Chicago and Denver. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: Zephyr service reached Denver May 31 1936 with the Advance Denver Zephyr on a 16-hour schedule, using the Pioneer Zephyr and Mark Twain Zephyr trainsets; the ten-car semi-articulated Denver Zephyr replaced them Nov 8 1936. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: The Ak-Sar-Ben Zephyr ('Nebraska' spelled backwards) began Dec 11 1940 running Chicago-Omaha-Lincoln, operating 1940-1947 and again 1953-1970, alongside the Denver Zephyr on the through route. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
